subject: Activation roadmap & prompt-eval sprint plan for ElmHealth trial
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Ng <claire@elmhealth.ai>, Daniel Park <daniel.park@elmhealth.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 14 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Activation roadmap & prompt-eval sprint plan for ElmHealth trial

Hi Claire / Daniel —

Thanks for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed activation roadmap so we have the same expectations for the 4-week trial. I tried to keep this tightly scoped to what we discussed; please flag anything missing.

High-level pain and goals (what you told us)
- Primary pain: long tail of clinical note normalization errors that cost manual review time (~15–20% of cases).
- Goal: reduce manual normalization by 50% on the top 3 note types and surface confidence scores for human-in-the-loop review.

Trial scope (what Redwood will deliver)
- Endpoint: hosted trial using a quantized Llama-variant with prompt orchestration tuned for clinical notes.
- Data: ElmHealth will provide a 30k-record sample (de-identified) for initial tuning and 2k labeled records for eval.
- Prompt/eval: Redwood will deliver a seed prompt-suite (attached) + evaluation harness and produce weekly quality reports.

Success metrics (mutually agreed)
- Precision@Top: >= 82% on normalization for target note types (week 4).
- Latency: P95 infer latency <= 450ms for 512-token requests under trial load.
- Cost goal: target < $0.012 per 1k output tokens for the trial environment (benchmarking run week 2).

Owners & communication
- Redwood lead: Mina Haddad (trial activation + eval owner)
- Platform POC: Rishi Malhotra (ops & scaling)
- ElmHealth POCs: Claire Ng (product), Daniel Park (data engineer)

Week-by-week sprint plan (proposed)
- Week 0 (now → Nov 18): access + infra setup (S3 read perms, API key or VPC peering, sample data shared).
- Week 1 (Nov 19–25): seed prompts + baseline run, initial tuning, and observability hook-ups.
- Week 2 (Nov 26–Dec 2): prompt iterations, regression checks, latency/cost baseline benchmarking.
- Week 3 (Dec 3–9): closed-loop eval on labeled set, human-in-the-loop UI review session.
- Week 4 (Dec 10–16): final report, acceptance review, optional next steps (Dedicated or Private deployment discussion).

Immediate asks (please deliver these this week)
- ElmHealth: provide AWS account ID and S3 bucket name + cross-account role ARN (or, if you prefer, we can do temporary presigned URLs).
- ElmHealth: share the 2k labeled sample and the data schema (PII redaction approach noted).
- ElmHealth: confirm the internal reviewers for the week-3 HIL session (name + email).

Attachments: elm-pilot-scope-v1.pdf (scope & SOW stub), prompt-suite-seed.csv (seed prompts / examples).

Next steps
- If this looks good, can we lock the technical kickoff for Wed Nov 17 at 11:00 AM PT? I’ll send a calendar invite and the onboarding runbook link.

Thanks — excited to get this running.

—
Mina Haddad
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0192
Redwood Inference
From: Claire Ng <claire@elmhealth.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Daniel Park <daniel.park@elmhealth.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 14 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Activation roadmap & prompt-eval sprint plan for ElmHealth trial

Thanks Mina — this is excellent, very aligned. A few follow-ups from our side:

1) Data schema & PII: attaching elm-data-schema.csv. We will de-identify PHI on our side but want to confirm what fields Redwood needs for evaluation (we can mask patient ids). Also: we use a hashed MRN; we need your guidance on whether that qualifies as de-identified for the Hosted trial.

2) AWS access: we can provide an IAM role for cross-account access. Daniel will provision and share the ARN by EOD Monday.

3) Latency expectations: 450ms P95 sounds reasonable; question on burst traffic — what guarantees can Redwood provide if we spike beyond the trial baseline during validation?

4) Technical kickoff: Wed Nov 17 11:00 AM PT works for us. Please include the infra checklist and any SSO/SCIM notes we need for user setup.

Attachment: elm-data-schema.csv (sample column list).

—
Claire Ng
Director, Product | ElmHealth
claire@elmhealth.ai
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Ng <claire@elmhealth.ai>, Daniel Park <daniel.park@elmhealth.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 14 Nov 2026 12:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Activation roadmap & prompt-eval sprint plan for ElmHealth trial

Claire — thanks for the quick notes, and good questions. Short answers inline below + details.

1) PII / hashed MRNs: hashed MRNs are OK for evaluation as long as they are non-reversible and consistently hashed across records. We will not attempt re-identification. We’ll include a short data handling addendum in the trial SOW that references our hosted trial controls.

2) AWS access: great — Daniel, when you share the ARN please also indicate whether the role has s3:GetObject and s3:ListBucket on the sample prefix. If you prefer presigned URLs for the initial run, we can accept that too.

3) Burst handling: for the Hosted trial we have a soft capacity of 2x baseline bursts; if you anticipate sustained higher throughput we should provision a short dedicated burst window. For the trial we’ll configure autoscaling + a fallback policy to a cheaper model variant to preserve throughput if we hit sustained constraints. I’ll add this to the kickoff agenda.

4) Kickoff: confirmed for Wed Nov 17, 11:00 AM PT. I’ll send a calendar invite with the onboarding runbook (link below) and a short infra checklist.

Runbook link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB_onboarding_runbook
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/5842/DN-4729

Action items (owners):
- Daniel (ElmHealth): share IAM role ARN + s3 prefix (by 2026-11-16 EOD)
- Claire (ElmHealth): confirm HIL reviewers for Week 3 (by 2026-11-19)
- Mina (Redwood): seed prompt-suite + eval harness (by 2026-11-20)
- Rishi (Redwood): configure trial autoscale & cost benchmarking job (by 2026-11-22)

Attachments referenced: prompt-suite-seed.csv (I’ll upload to the Drive folder).

Talk soon — I’ll invite the team.

—
Mina Haddad
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.ai
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Claire Ng <claire@elmhealth.ai>
Date: Sat, 14 Nov 2026 17:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Activation roadmap & prompt-eval sprint plan for ElmHealth trial

Looping in quickly — this plan looks good. A couple internal notes:

- Mina: I’ll pre-provision a trial autoscale profile tuned to the sample distribution you sent; I’ll post the baseline cost estimate in the Drive folder by Monday.
- Marissa: can you flag if the deal team wants us to offer a pilot credit or a one-time onboarding credit? ElmHealth is mid-market but shows strong potential for Dedicated this year.

Claire — we’ll keep the burst fallback conservative for the first two weeks, then revisit after the week-2 benchmark run. If you have an expected max TPS for validation traffic, please share and we’ll simulate ahead of kickoff.

Thanks everyone — Mina, I’ll join the kickoff on Wed.

—
Rishi Malhotra
Staff Site Reliability Engineer | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
